# Security policy

## Supported version

Security fixes are provided in the latest published preview, currently **v0.4.3**. Update from older previews using the [Windows installer, portable ZIP or experimental macOS/Ubuntu archives](https://github.com/maamouribilel/pc-remote/releases/tag/v0.4.3). Versions 0.3.0 and later bundle .NET 10.0.13 from Microsoft's 2026-10-13 security release; earlier builds bundle the affected 10.0.12 runtime. From v0.4.3 the companion can check for updates after asking once (see `AUTO_UPDATE_PLAN.md`); versions up to v0.4.2 never check, so update them by hand, or choose **Watch → Custom → Releases** on GitHub to be notified. Preview status and outstanding physical/manual acceptance checks are documented in release notes, `docs/release-checklist.md` and `docs/release-readiness.md`. The macOS and Ubuntu builds are experimental: report issues for them the same way, but they do not yet have the native and physical acceptance evidence of the Windows companion.

## Report an issue privately

Use [GitHub's private vulnerability report form](https://github.com/maamouribilel/pc-remote/security/advisories/new) or the repository's **Security → Report a vulnerability** button. Include the affected version, a minimal reproduction, expected/observed behavior, and relevant operating system/browser details. Use test data; omit credentials, private keys, pairing links, cookies, personal paths, and network addresses. Keep exploitable details out of public issues until a fix is available.

## Trust boundaries

- Pair only your own trusted browser and approve only a request you initiated. An approved browser can control applications in your signed-in desktop session on Windows, macOS or Ubuntu; keyboard access is broad access, even though individual API commands are allowlisted.
- Use a trusted Private LAN, the companion's displayed HTTPS address, certificate fingerprint verification, and the scoped Private/LocalSubnet firewall rule. Do not expose TCP 8443 to the internet or bypass certificate warnings.
- Device credentials and private certificate keys use Windows-user DPAPI and restricted local storage. This protects them from other normal Windows users; it cannot protect a Windows account already compromised by malware or an administrator.
- Revoke lost browsers in the companion and use **Pause control** or **Exit** (tray on Windows and Ubuntu, menu bar on macOS) to stop control. Remembered browser authorization lasts up to 30 days. Remove certificate trust when permanently retiring an installation.
- On macOS, the storage key lives in the per-user login Keychain and certificate/device files are AES-256-GCM envelopes. On Ubuntu, the key lives in the password-encrypted GNOME login keyring, which is weaker than DPAPI/Keychain against same-user access. See the platform guides.
- Update checks (since 0.4.3) are off until the person agrees or presses **Check now**. They contact only GitHub over HTTPS, send no device, pairing or setting data, and never download or run an installer. A release is shown only when its `update.json` verifies against the offline release key embedded in the app; that private key never enters the repository, CI or GitHub. Someone controlling the GitHub account but not that key cannot make a companion announce or install a release.
- On a Windows installer copy (since 0.4.3), **Download update** fetches only the installer named in the re-verified signed manifest and checks its exact size and SHA-256; **Restart to update** runs it silently. The downloaded installer is unsigned and carries no download mark, so SmartScreen may not check it (not yet observed on Windows); the manifest signature is the gate the companion relies on, so protect the release key accordingly. The verified file stays open with read-only sharing until the installer starts. Portable, macOS and Ubuntu copies only notify.
- Releases are unsigned (macOS bundles carry only a local ad-hoc seal; no Developer ID/notarization or Linux distribution signature). Obtain assets from this repository's GitHub Releases and compare their SHA-256 hashes; source archives are not installed applications.

## Verification

`scripts/test.ps1 -Security` exercises real certificate-validated HTTPS against an isolated loopback server with recording input/power adapters. It checks unauthorized mutations, browser-origin restrictions, private-file isolation, request limits, safety-action capacity, and ownership changes during delayed media requests. Other suites cover pairing, WebSocket validation/replay/cleanup, lifecycle, and browser interaction.

`scripts/audit-dependencies.ps1` checks npm and NuGet feeds. GitHub's **Security and regression checks** workflow runs the automated suites and dependency audits on pull requests, on manual dispatch and, as the release gate, on the `final` dispatch for each version. Release preparation also scans secrets and verifies bundled runtime advisories, package contents, licenses, and public asset hashes. Passing checks reduce known risks; they do not establish that the app has no bugs or replace physical-device/manual acceptance.

`scripts/test-certificate.ps1` uses Python 3.13+ with strict chain/name verification, including negative trust tests. Existing server leaves missing authority/subject key identifiers are renewed on upgrade while keeping the trusted root. No production certificate-verification bypass is introduced.

## Portable foundation (development)

The shared host now requires explicit platform services; production WPF startup still uses Windows DPAPI, restricted ACLs, real Windows input/actions and Private-network discovery. There is no production plaintext protection fallback. Shared certificate issuance is independent of OS storage/key loading, retaining Windows protected-file formats and leaf-only renewal.

`tests/PcController.PortableTests` contains loopback recording adapters and temporary test storage, with no normal startup path. `python3 scripts/portable.py test` checks pairing/ownership/transport/security/cleanup; `tls` requires Python 3.13+ and verifies strict chain/name acceptance and rejection. CI defines shared checks on Windows/macOS/Linux and retains Windows-specific regressions. Actual new platform results belong in `MULTIPLATFORM_PLAN.md`; job configuration and cross-compilation do not prove Windows DPAPI/native behavior or phone/LAN acceptance. Future Mac/Linux production stores and explicit network approval remain prerequisites.

Phase 2 adds an Avalonia development shell and capability-aware browser. Normal Mac/Linux startup has no host listener until reviewed platform secure storage is implemented; no production recording/plaintext fallback exists. Network approval is session-only and invalidated on detected connectivity/identity changes, with old listeners stopped. Platform-native network identity/notification coverage and LAN acceptance remain prerequisites for production startup. Backend capabilities reject unavailable actions independently of browser presentation. Session claims reauthorize after body reads; shutdown denies late pairing approvals; failed revocation retains pause. See `docs/desktop-shell.md` for fixture boundaries and native/manual gaps.

## Phase 3 macOS source candidate

The source-built Mac companion uses real Accessibility-gated Quartz input and a default per-user file-based Keychain encryption key, with path-authenticated AES-256-GCM certificate/device envelopes and 0700/0600 per-user files. No plaintext/System Keychain fallback, implicit unlock, root execution, automatic trust installation or unrelated permission request is introduced. Locked/unavailable storage stops listening; missing keys/roots and authenticated-envelope corruption require explicit recovery. Same-user compromise/admin access remains outside the storage boundary. The unsigned candidate's ACL/TCC identity after rebuild and eventual signing needs manual acceptance.

LAN approval explicitly selects an interface/connectivity session; SystemConfiguration, address/availability, system sleep/wake and session-switch events invalidate it and native generation checks block raced input. Space/full-screen, display and Secure Input/permission transitions pause control and release input but keep the session's LAN approval; per-event console, Secure Input, login-window and armed-generation checks still block input to locked or secure targets. Redacted Wi-Fi names do not request Location or authenticate the network; same-subnet roaming/route/cable-change notification coverage needs real acceptance before relying on LAN operation. AppKit lifecycle plus public Accessibility/session/Secure Input checks pause remote input; physical lock/suspend behavior remains a supervised check. Cleanup failures preserve tracking, prevent Resume and keep graceful Exit open. macOS media/volume/launcher/power remain unavailable. Since version 0.3.0, releases publish this companion as an experimental macOS archive; [macOS guide](../docs/macos-setup.md) and the roadmap separate Keychain/TLS evidence from native and phone acceptance.

## Phase 4 Linux candidate (2026-10-13)

Linux source startup now uses real XCB/XTEST or explicit GNOME RemoteDesktop portal consent, reviewed encrypted persistent GNOME login-keyring storage, local lifecycle/network monitoring and per-user instance lock. It starts paused, requires explicit session LAN approval, stops listeners on storage failure and retains failed input cleanup. Text defaults unavailable until local GTK Unicode opt-in; it is target-specific. Interrupted composition or unreachable ended-session holds need verified local recovery; that is not automatic cleanup evidence. Media/volume/launcher/power/start-at-login remain unavailable.

Phase 4 remains **In progress**: actual Ubuntu 24.04 x64/GNOME X11 and Wayland Unicode/shortcut/permission-loss/cleanup/lock/suspend/tray/roaming checks and strict physical-phone/LAN acceptance are pending. Xvfb and fake-portal checks cannot establish those gates. Secret Service is not DPAPI-equivalent; blank-password/plaintext, locked/missing and unreviewed providers fail. Read [Linux prerequisites, storage properties, recovery and support matrix](../docs/linux-setup.md). Since version 0.3.0, releases publish an experimental Ubuntu 24.04 x64 archive; Windows remains the primary platform.


## Phase 5 source candidates (2026-10-13)

Supported native feature adapters and packages are described in [the release-readiness handoff](../docs/release-readiness.md). Since version 0.3.0, releases publish them as experimental macOS/Ubuntu archives alongside the Windows companion. Mac Core Audio/native system media/player shortcuts/LaunchServices/login registration/sleep and Linux libpulse/MPRIS/player shortcuts/restricted GIO/XDG/logind use real platform services with backend denial and final native readiness/permission checks. Mac restart/shutdown stay unavailable; Linux power requires `Can* == yes`, `interactive=false`, no inhibitor override. Launcher wire input is still configured IDs only; no remote path/arguments/shell. Native dependencies/signing/login eligibility/actual player and physical power acceptance remain separate from recording/source-table/protocol/package checks.

Readiness transitions now force replacement of the capability snapshot even on unchanged loopback bindings; old ownership/listeners stop and replacement starts paused. v1 fields, budgets/reserved cancellation, original-session authentication checks, device-bound confirmation/countdown/cancellation and failed cleanup retention remain. Optional login start never preserves LAN approval/Wayland consent or resumes control. Provisional manifests record version/base revision/dirty source/file hashes; no tag/public release is created. Windows adapters, DPAPI and packaging remain intact. Real GNOME/phone/LAN/installed/Intel/CI gates stay visible.


PC mutations now capture the original connected session before reading a body. Chunked-body tests reject attempts to finish old volume/launcher/power requests using a replacement session ID or ticket. Authentication remains rechecked inside the ownership lock, and cancellation retains its reserved quota. Legacy Mac Keychain reads explicitly suppress UI interaction so denied ACL/signing access cannot leave startup/Exit waiting for an implicit prompt; denied storage stops listeners and never resets roots/keys. Because each unsigned build has a new ad-hoc code identity, only the explicit local **Allow Keychain access after update…** action permits macOS's own Keychain dialog for the existing key. The user approves it with the login Keychain password; the app never edits the access list, unlocks the Keychain or replaces keys. Background reads fail closed while that request is open.
